questions.question: How many players does a basketball team have on court?
questions.fact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith, using peach baskets as hoops. Players had to climb up to get the ball back.

questions.question: Which country has won the most men's FIFA World Cups?
questions.fact: Brazil has won the World Cup five times and is the only country to have played in every men's World Cup.

questions.question: In tennis, what is a score of zero called?
questions.fact: One popular theory is that "love" comes from "l'œuf", French for "the egg", because a zero looks like an egg.

questions.question: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.fact: The five rings stand for the continents taking part, and every national flag contains at least one of the ring colours.

questions.question: Which sport uses a shuttlecock?
questions.fact: A shuttlecock is traditionally made with 16 goose feathers, and smashes can fly at over 400 km/h.

questions.question: How long is a marathon?
questions.fact: The marathon is named after the legend of a Greek messenger who ran from Marathon to Athens to announce a victory.

questions.question: Which Spanish tennis player won the French Open 14 times?
questions.fact: Nadal's 14 French Open titles are the most any player has won at a single Grand Slam tournament.

questions.question: Which football club plays at the Camp Nou?
questions.fact: Camp Nou opened in 1957 and is the biggest football stadium in Europe. "Camp Nou" simply means "new field" in Catalan.

questions.question: What is Real Madrid's home stadium called?
questions.fact: The Bernabéu is named after Santiago Bernabéu, Real Madrid's player and later president for 35 years.

questions.question: In which sport would you do a slam dunk?
questions.fact: The term "slam dunk" is said to have been coined by the commentator of the Los Angeles Lakers, Chick Hearn.

questions.question: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.fact: Golf rounds have 18 holes because the Old Course at St Andrews, in Scotland, settled on 18 back in 1764.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 2010 World Cup, which Spain won?
questions.fact: The 2010 World Cup was the first ever held in Africa, famous for the loud vuvuzela horns.

questions.question: Who scored Spain's winning goal in the 2010 World Cup final?
questions.fact: Iniesta scored in the 116th minute of extra time against the Netherlands, and Spain won 1–0.

questions.question: What is the highest possible score in one game of ten-pin bowling?
questions.fact: A perfect 300 game needs 12 strikes in a row.

questions.question: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football?
questions.fact: After a touchdown, the team can try for 1 extra point with a kick or 2 points with another play.

questions.question: Which sport is played at Wimbledon?
questions.fact: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world, first played in 1877. Players must wear almost all white.

questions.question: How many players does a volleyball team have on court?
questions.fact: Volleyball was invented in 1895 in the USA, as a gentler game than basketball.

questions.question: Which Argentine footballer won the 2022 World Cup after many years at Barcelona?
questions.fact: Messi has won the Ballon d'Or a record eight times.

questions.question: Cristiano Ronaldo is from which country?
questions.fact: Cristiano Ronaldo is the top goalscorer in men's international football, with well over 100 goals for Portugal.

questions.question: Which country did judo come from?
questions.fact: Judo means "the gentle way". It was created by Kanō Jigorō in 1882 and became an Olympic sport in 1964.

questions.question: What is the most famous cycling race in France called?
questions.fact: The Tour de France started in 1903, to sell more copies of a sports newspaper.

questions.question: What is Spain's big three-week cycling race called?
questions.fact: La Vuelta a España was first held in 1935. Its leader wears a red jersey, "la roja".

questions.question: How many minutes does a football match last, without extra time?
questions.fact: The extra minutes at the end of each half are called "stoppage time" or "added time".

questions.question: In football, where may the goalkeeper handle the ball?
questions.fact: Since 1992, goalkeepers may not pick up a ball deliberately passed back to them by a teammate's foot.

questions.question: Which sport is Usain Bolt famous for?
questions.fact: Usain Bolt's 100 m world record is 9.58 seconds, set in Berlin in 2009.

questions.question: Which swimmer won 23 Olympic gold medals?
questions.fact: Michael Phelps won 28 Olympic medals in total, more than any other athlete in history.

questions.question: In which sport is a "puck" used?
questions.fact: Ice hockey pucks are frozen before games so they slide faster and bounce less.

questions.question: What colour jersey does the leader of the Tour de France wear?
questions.fact: The yellow jersey matched the yellow paper of "L'Auto", the newspaper that started the Tour.

questions.question: What colour jersey does the leader of the Giro d'Italia wear?
questions.fact: The pink jersey matches the pink pages of La Gazzetta dello Sport, the newspaper that started the Giro.

questions.question: Which country won the Euro 2024 football championship?
questions.fact: Spain beat England 2–1 in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin, winning all seven of its games.

questions.question: How many men's European Championships had Spain won by the end of 2024?
questions.fact: Spain won the Euros in 1964, 2008, 2012 and 2024, more than any other country.

questions.question: How many points is a basketball shot from behind the arc worth?
questions.fact: The three-point line was added to the NBA in 1979.

questions.question: Which sport has positions called scrum-half and fly-half?
questions.fact: Rugby is said to have started in 1823 when a pupil at Rugby School picked up the ball and ran with it.

questions.question: How many players does a rugby union team have on the field?
questions.fact: Rugby league, a different version of the sport, has 13 players per team instead of 15.

questions.question: Which Spanish driver won the Formula 1 World Championship twice?
questions.fact: Fernando Alonso won his titles in 2005 and 2006 with Renault, ending Michael Schumacher's run of five titles.

questions.question: In which town are the streets of the Monaco Grand Prix?
questions.fact: The Monaco Grand Prix is one of the slowest, tightest races of the year, and overtaking there is famously hard.

questions.question: In golf, what do you call one under par on a hole?
questions.fact: Two under par is an "eagle", three under is an "albatross", and one over is a "bogey".

questions.question: How often are the Summer Olympics usually held?
questions.fact: The Winter Olympics are also every four years, two years after each Summer Games.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics?
questions.fact: Paris also hosted the Olympics in 1900 and 1924, so 2024 was its third time.

questions.question: Which city will host the 2028 Summer Olympics?
questions.fact: Los Angeles will host the Summer Olympics for the third time in 2028, after 1932 and 1984.

questions.question: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on clay?
questions.fact: The French Open is played at Roland Garros, named after a French aviator, on red clay made of crushed brick.

questions.question: Who is the all-time top scorer for Spain's men's national team?
questions.fact: David Villa scored 59 goals for Spain and was top scorer at Euro 2008.

questions.question: What does "MVP" stand for?
questions.fact: MVP awards are given in most team sports, like the NBA Finals MVP in basketball.

questions.question: Which boxer called himself "The Greatest"?
questions.fact: Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay and won Olympic gold in 1960 before turning professional.

questions.question: Which sport takes place in a velodrome?
questions.fact: Velodrome tracks are steeply banked, up to about 45 degrees on the bends.

questions.question: What is it called when one player scores three goals in a game?
questions.fact: The name comes from cricket, where a bowler who took three wickets in a row was given a new hat.

questions.question: Which country is home to the sport of hurling?
questions.fact: Hurling is one of the oldest field games in the world, played with a wooden stick and a small ball.

questions.question: What is the name of Chicago's NBA team?
questions.fact: With Michael Jordan, the Chicago Bulls won six NBA titles in the 1990s.

questions.question: Pau Gasol won NBA titles with which team?
questions.fact: Pau Gasol won two NBA titles with the Lakers, in 2009 and 2010, alongside Kobe Bryant.

questions.question: How many players does a water polo team have in the water?
questions.fact: Water polo players aren't allowed to touch the bottom of the pool, so they tread water the whole game.

questions.question: Basketball was invented in which country?
questions.fact: Basketball was invented in Massachusetts, but by a Canadian, James Naismith.

questions.question: A "home run" is part of which sport?
questions.fact: A home run hit with the bases loaded, scoring four runs, is called a "grand slam".

questions.question: Which man has won the most Grand Slam singles titles in tennis?
questions.fact: Novak Djokovic has won 24 Grand Slam singles titles, more than any other man.

questions.question: Which young Spanish player won Wimbledon in both 2023 and 2024?
questions.fact: Carlos Alcaraz, from Murcia, became world number 1 at just 19, the youngest man ever to do it.

questions.question: In football, which card means a player is sent off?
questions.fact: Red and yellow cards were introduced at the 1970 World Cup, inspired by traffic lights.

questions.question: The Ballon d'Or is an award in which sport?
questions.fact: The Ballon d'Or, "golden ball", has been awarded by France Football magazine since 1956.

questions.question: What is the most sets a men's Grand Slam match can have?
questions.fact: The longest tennis match ever lasted 11 hours and 5 minutes, at Wimbledon in 2010.

questions.question: Which martial art's name means "the way of the empty hand"?
questions.fact: Karate developed in Okinawa, Japan, and became an Olympic sport for the first time at Tokyo 2020.

questions.question: Which sport is Simone Biles famous for?
questions.fact: Simone Biles has several gymnastics moves officially named after her.

questions.question: "El Clásico" is a match between Real Madrid and…
questions.fact: Real Madrid and Barcelona have played each other well over 250 times in competitive matches.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 1982 World Cup?
questions.fact: Italy won the 1982 World Cup in Spain, beating West Germany 3–1 in the final at the Bernabéu.
